agent_assessment: The research conclusion is thorough, well-structured, and answers the research question comprehensively. It defines a unified release record model across deployment-manager, LPBS, and scenario-to-desktop with clear canonical IDs, schemas, Go types, and promotion semantics. However, codebase verification reveals several factual inaccuracies: (1) Migration 004 already exists in DM (adds git_commit_hash to visual_validations), so the proposed releases migration should be 005, not 004. (2) Line number references are consistently off by 10-40 lines (DeployDesktopRequest is at lines 21-51 not 24-55, CheckReleaseGate at 193-234 not 183-224, channelToVariantKey at lines 89-94 not 50-55, UpsertAsset variant_key at line 573 not 596). (3) DeployDesktopRequest has 14 fields, not 15. (4) The LPBS UpsertAsset already has a VariantKey field with default fallback logic — the conclusion describes this as 'hardcoded' but it is already parameterized with a default. These are minor factual drifts likely caused by code changes after the research rounds, but implementers relying on exact line numbers or migration numbers would hit friction. The 7 proposed action items are concrete, well-prioritized, and correctly scoped. GCT results for deployment-manager (168 code quality violations, 2 test failures, 41 standards warnings) are pre-existing and unrelated to this research item.
notes: Migration numbering is stale: DM migration 004 already exists (004_add_validation_commit_hash.sql). The proposed releases migration should target 005.

Line number references across all 4 verified locations are off by 10-40 lines. Functions and structs exist at the correct files but shifted positions, likely due to code changes after the research was written.
DeployDesktopRequest has 14 fields (not 15 as stated). GitCommitHash may have been the 14th added after the initial count.

LPBS UpsertAsset variant_key is already parameterized (asset.VariantKey with '' -> 'default' fallback at line 573), not hardcoded as the conclusion implies. Action 4 may already be partially addressed.

The download_artifacts table referenced in LPBS code may have schema drift — the initialization SQL schema and the runtime code reference different column sets. Implementers should verify the actual DB state before adding release_id.
GCT code quality (0.0 score, 168 violations) and test failures (2/11) for deployment-manager are pre-existing conditions, not caused by this research item.

evidence.title: Conclusion completeness — research question coverage
evidence.description: The conclusion addresses all aspects of the research question: canonical IDs (UUID minted by DM orchestrator), references (release_id correlation across DM/LPBS/S2D), schema shape (releases + release_platforms tables with full DDL), channel model (nightly/beta/stable with promotion semantics), and approval interaction (commit-scoped, no channel dimension). 16 findings cover the full design space. 7 action items map to concrete backlog entries with kind, priority, effort, and initiative tags.

improvement_suggestions.description: Research conclusions should use relative references (function names, struct names) as primary identifiers rather than absolute line numbers, since line numbers drift as code evolves. Line numbers can be included as supplementary hints but should not be the sole locator.

Add a pre-review step for research items that re-verifies codebase references (migration numbers, line numbers, field counts) against the current state, flagging any drift since the research was conducted.
